cues.en: Human existence is scary and confusing. A few hundred thousand years ago, we became conscious and found ourselves in a strange place. It was filled with other beings. We could eat some, some could eat us. There was liquid stuff we could drink, things we could use to make more things. The daytime sky had a tiny yellow ball that warmed our skin. The night sky was filled with beautiful lights. This place was obviously made for us. Something was watching over us. We were home.
cues.zh: 人类的存在让人恐惧又困惑。几十万年前，我们产生了意识，发现自己置身于一个陌生的地方。这里到处都是其他生物。有些能被我们吃掉，有些则会吃掉我们。这里有可以喝的液体，也有能用来制造更多东西的材料。白天的天空挂着一颗温暖我们皮肤的小黄球。夜晚的天空则布满了美丽的亮光。这个地方显然是为我们而造的。有某种存在一直在照看着我们。我们就像待在家里一样。

cues.en: This made everything much less scary and confusing. But the older we got, the more we learned about the world and ourselves. We learned that the twinkling lights are not shining beautifully for us, they just are. We learned that we're not at the center of what we now call the universe, and that it is much, much older than we thought. We learned that we're made of many little dead things, which make up bigger things that are not dead for some reason. And that we're just another temporary stage in a history going back over a billion years.
cues.zh: 这让一切都没那么吓人，也没那么让人困惑了。但随着我们不断成长，我们对世界和自身有了更多的了解。我们发现，那些闪烁的微光并不是在为我们绽放美丽，它们只是客观存在着。我们发现，我们并不是如今所谓的宇宙的中心，而且宇宙比我们想象的要古老得多得多。我们发现，我们是由许多无生命的微小物质构成的，不知为何，它们组合成了更大的、有生命的实体。而且在长达十亿多年的历史长河中，我们不过是又一个短暂的阶段。

cues.en: We learned, in all, that we live on a moist speck of dust moving around a medium-sized star in a quiet region of one arm of an average galaxy, which is part of a galaxy group that we will never leave. And this group is only one of thousands that together make up a galaxy supercluster. But even our supercluster is only one in thousands that make up what we call the observable universe. The universe might be a million times bigger, but we will never know.
cues.zh: 总而言之，我们认识到，自己生活在一粒潮湿的尘埃上，围绕着一颗中等大小的恒星运转，位于一个普通星系某条旋臂的宁静角落，而这个星系又是我们永远无法离开的星系群的一部分。这个星系群也仅仅是构成超星系团的数千个星系群之一。但即便连我们的超星系团，也只是构成所谓“可观测宇宙”的数千个超星系团之一。宇宙可能比这还要大上一百万倍，但我们永远无法知晓。

cues.en: We could throw words around like 200 billion galaxies or trillions of stars or bazillions of planets, but all of these numbers mean nothing. Our brains can't comprehend these concepts. The universe is too big. There is too much of it. But size is not the most troubling concept we have to deal with. It's time, or more precisely, the time we have. If you're lucky enough to live to 100, you have 5,200 weeks at your disposal. If you're 25 now,
cues.zh: 我们可以随意说出两千亿个星系、数万亿颗恒星或无数颗行星这样的词，但所有这些数字毫无意义。我们的大脑根本无法理解这些概念。宇宙太大了。它包含的内容太多了。但大小并不是我们必须面对的最让人不安的概念。最让人不安的是时间，或者更确切地说，是我们所拥有的时间。如果你有幸活到100岁，你手头支配的时间也就是5200个星期。如果你现在25岁，

cues.en: Then you have 3,900 weeks left. If you're going to die at 70, then there are 2,340 weeks left. A lot of time, but also... not really. And then what? Your biological processes will break down, and the dynamic pattern that is you will stop being dynamic. It will dissolve until there is no you left. Some believe that there is a part of us we can't see or measure, but we have no way to find out. So...
cues.zh: 那你还剩下3900个星期。如果你在70岁去世，那就只剩下2340个星期了。看似很长的时间，其实……并不长。那之后又会怎样呢？你的生理机能会瓦解，属于你的动态模式将不再运转。它会逐渐消解，直到不留下任何关于你的痕迹。有些人相信，我们身上有一部分是看不见、测不出的，但我们无从查证。所以……

cues.en: This life might be it, and we might end up dead forever. This is less scary than it sounds, though. If you don't remember the 13.75 billion years that went by before you existed, then the trillions and trillions and trillions of years that come after will pass in no time once you're gone. Close your eyes. Count to one. That's how long forever feels. And as far as we know, in the end, the universe itself will die, and nothing will ever change again.
cues.zh: 可能这一生就是全部了，我们最终会永远死去。不过，这其实没有听起来那么可怕。如果你完全不记得自己存在之前的137.5亿年，那么等你离去之后，接下来的千万亿年也同样会一瞬而过。闭上眼睛。数到一。永恒的感觉不过如此。而且据我们所知，宇宙本身最终也会走向消亡，从此再也不会有任何改变。

cues.en: Our videos induce existential dread in many people, and the last few minutes probably haven't helped. So, for once, we want to offer a different way of looking at these things. An unscientific, subjective point of view. The philosophy of Kurzgesagt, if you want. Please take it with a grain of salt. We don't know any more about human existence than you do. We counter existential dread with optimistic nihilism. What do we mean by that? Well, to summarize,
cues.zh: 我们的视频让很多人产生存在性恐惧，而最后几分钟大概也没帮上忙。所以这次，我们想提供一种不同的看待方式。一种不科学、主观的视角。也可以说是 Kurzgesagt 的哲学。请姑且听之，别太当真。关于人类存在，我们并不比你懂更多。我们用乐观虚无主义对抗存在性恐惧。这是什么意思？简单总结一下，

cues.en: It seems very unlikely that 200 trillion trillion stars have been made for us. In a way, it feels like the cruelest joke in existence has been played on us. We became self-aware, only to realize this story is not about us. While it is great to know about electrons in the powerhouse of the cell, science doesn't do a lot to make this less depressing. Okay, but so what? You only get one shot at life, which is scary, but it also sets you free. If the universe ends in heat death,
cues.zh: 200万亿万亿颗恒星似乎不太可能是为我们而造的。某种意义上，感觉就像宇宙对我们开了最残酷的玩笑。我们有了自我意识，却意识到这个故事不是关于我们的。虽然知道细胞动力工厂里的电子很棒，但科学并不能让这一切没那么压抑。好吧，但那又怎样？人生只有一次，这很可怕，但也让你自由。如果宇宙最终走向热寂，

cues.en: Every humiliation you suffer in your life will be forgotten. Every mistake you made will not matter in the end. Every bad thing you did will be voided. If our life is all we get to experience, then it's the only thing that matters. If the universe has no principles, the only principles relevant are the ones we decide on. If the universe has no purpose, then we get to dictate what its purpose is. Humans will most certainly cease to exist at some point. But before we do,
cues.zh: 你一生中遭受的每一次羞辱都会被遗忘。你犯过的每一个错误最终都不重要。你做过的每件坏事都会被一笔勾销。如果人生是我们唯一能体验的东西，那它就是唯一重要的事。如果宇宙没有原则，唯一相关的原则就是我们自己选定的。如果宇宙没有目的，那它的目的就由我们来规定。人类几乎肯定会在某个时刻不复存在。但在那之前，

cues.en: We get to explore ourselves and the world around us. We get to experience feelings. We get to experience food, books, sunrises, and being with each other. The fact that we're even able to think about these things is already kind of incredible. It's easy to think of ourselves as separated from everything, but this is not true. We are as much the universe as a neutron star, or a black hole, or a nebula. Even better actually, we are its thinking and feeling part.
cues.zh: 我们可以探索自己和周围的世界。我们可以体验感受。我们可以体验食物、书、日出，还有彼此相伴。我们甚至能思考这些事情，本身就已经很不可思议。我们很容易觉得自己与一切分离，但这不是真的。我们和中子星、黑洞或星云一样，都是宇宙本身。甚至更妙的是，我们还是它思考和感受的部分。

cues.en: the sensory organs of the universe. We are truly free in a universe-sized playground, so we might as well aim to be happy and to build some kind of utopia in the stars. It's not as if we found out everything there is to know. We don't know why the rules of the universe are as they are, how life came into existence, what life is. We have no idea what consciousness is or if we are alone in the universe, but we can try to find some answers. There are billions of stars to visit,
cues.zh: 是宇宙的感觉器官。我们身处宇宙大小的游乐场，真正自由，所以不妨以快乐为目标，在群星间建造某种乌托邦。并不是说我们已经弄清了所有该知道的事。我们不知道宇宙法则为何如此，生命如何出现，生命是什么。我们不知道意识是什么，也不知道宇宙中我们是否孤独，但我们可以试着找些答案。有数十亿颗恒星等着我们去探访，

cues.en: diseases to cure, people to help, happy feelings to be experienced, and video games to finish. There is so much to do. So wrapping up, you've probably used up a good chunk of the time available to you. If this is our one shot at life, there is no reason not to have fun and live as happily as possible. Bonus points if you make the life of other people better. More bonus points if you help build a galactic human empire. Do the things that make you feel good.
cues.zh: 有疾病要治愈，有人要帮助，有快乐要体验，还有电子游戏要通关。有太多事可做。总结一下，你可能已经用掉了可用时间的一大部分。如果人生只有这一次，那就没有理由不尽情玩、尽可能快乐地活。如果你让别人的人生更好，那就加分。如果你帮忙建立银河人类帝国，再加分。去做让你感觉好的事。

cues.en: You get to decide whatever this means for you. It's time to reveal our darkest secret. This may come as a surprise to you, but Klotzgesagt is not actually run by burbs, but by humans. Now you might wonder, how's this possible? So many people spending hundreds of hours on research, writing and animating the Klotzgesagt videos that are then released for free. Well, the answer is simple. It's possible because of our shop.
cues.zh: 你可以自己决定这对你意味着什么。是时候揭晓我们最深藏的秘密了。这可能会让你感到意外，但 Klotzgesagt 实际上并不是由小鸟运营的，而是由人类运营的。现在你可能会好奇，这怎么可能呢？这么多人投入数百小时进行调研、撰写脚本并制作 Klotzgesagt 的动画视频，然后全部免费发布。好吧，答案其实很简单。这都多亏了我们的周边商店。

cues.en: Our products are a piece of Kurzgesagt that you can touch, read and have around you. Just like our videos, they're a vital part of our dream to inspire people all around the world. Our carefully researched infographic posters are now part of so many people's homes teaching them about evolution, black holes and the night sky. While our gratitude journal helps improve lives every day. A special thanks goes out to everyone who appreciates our weirder product ideas.
cues.zh: 我们的周边产品就像是你可以触碰、阅读并陪伴在身边的 Kurzgesagt。就像我们的视频一样，它们也是我们启发全世界观众这一梦想中至关重要的一部分。我们精心调研的信息图表海报，如今已经走进了许多人的家中，向他们展示着进化、黑洞和夜空的奥秘。而我们的感恩日志也在每天帮助大家改善生活。特别感谢每一位喜欢我们那些古怪产品创意的朋友。

cues.en: Every Kurzgesagt product you buy directly funds another moment we get to spend working on our videos, and you get a special piece of Kurzgesagt in return. Thank you so much for being a part of our story and for making this channel possible. The burp humans of Kurzgesagt are eternally grateful.
cues.zh: 你购买的每一件 Kurzgesagt 产品，都会直接支持我们投入更多时间来制作视频，而你也能获得一份属于自己的 Kurzgesagt 专属纪念。非常感谢大家成为我们故事的一部分，让这个频道能够一直走下去。Kurzgesagt 的“小鸟”人类对此永远心存感激。
